item.title: COMING Thursday, Nov 12 | Bluegrass and BBQ ft. The JackTown Ramblers — Sun Nov 1 — The Farm – A Gathering Place
item.description:
Thursday November 12 | Doors open at 5pm, Dinner 6 pm, Music 7-9 pm | $59.95 Event Details and Tickets Smoked BBQ, warm cornbread, and the JackTown Ramblers playing all night, fifteen minutes from downtown Asheville.
When the evenings turn cool in the mountains, this is the kind of dinner we want to gather around. Smoked BBQ chicken. Fried catfish with remoulade. Cornbread muffins with honey butter, still warm from the oven. Banana pudding to finish. It’s the food these hills are known for, cooked by the Farm Kitchen and passed down the table.
Live bluegrass from the JackTown Ramblers The JackTown Ramblers are a four-piece string band from western North Carolina. Their sets blend traditional bluegrass with swing tunes, a little gypsy jazz, and songs of their own, and they’ve become a familiar name on stages across the region.

item.title: Rattle Creek BBQ Food Truck — Sun Nov 1, 12:00 PM
item.description:
Rattle Creek BBQ is a smoked-meat food truck, bringing Cali-Mex meets Texas BBQ cooking to the mountains.
Before Asheville, owner Mat cooked in Austin, where he picked up a deep respect for low-and-slow brisket and a love for bright, fresh food creating the ultimate balanced meal. Rattle Creek’s menu includes BBQ plates, sandwiches, and tacos, featuring brisket, spare ribs, and pulled pork, plus sides like guajillo crunch slaw, elote corn salad, and queso mac & cheese.

item.title: Jack’s Traditional Irish/Celtic Jam Session — Sun Nov 1, 3:30 PM — Jack Of The Wood
item.description:
Stop in for the pub’s long running Traditional Irish Session each Sunday afternoon beginning around 3:30pm. Many talented local musicians come from WNC to jam away into the night – all on our pub stage! Sunday is a perfect day to enjoy a pint or afternoon Irish coffee! Slaínte! Jack Of The Wood is still a downtown hot spot for food, brews and drink since 1997 and founders Joan and Joe Eckert who still own it, have maintained the original lively English and Irish vibe. The old-time mountain and Irish music jams continue, including a hot bluegrass jam Thursdays and brunch every Sunday. The venue extends a welcoming feeling to regulars and newcomers to this day. https://jackofthewood.com/
Source: LiveMusicAsheville.com

item.title: The Big Asheville Science Salon! — Wed Nov 4, 6:00 PM
item.description:
Welcome to the tremendous, amazing, Big Asheville Science Salon! Next Month’s Salon Details Coming Soon! Our mission: Cultivate curiosity and build community by sharing the coolest, grooviest, and fascinating-ist scientific discoveries. And have a beer (or wine or soda). How it do: Each month, a bona fide expert takes us on a thrill ride of science awesomeness (i.e., talk about their research and probably show pretty pictures). Afterwards, a lively Q&A segues into general mingling and chatting about why science is so cool. When: First Wednesday of each month. Doors: 6:00pm; Presentation: 7:00pm; Socializing: 8:00pm Where: The Mule (at Devil’s Foot Beverage) 131 Sweeten Creek Rd., Asheville, NC 28803 No cover charge – just bring your brain! Doors open at 5:00. Have a drink with old friends, meet new ones, and get ready for some serious science in a seriously un-serious setting.
Source: The Mule at Devils Foot

item.title: Grand Opening Rattle Creek BBQ Food Truck — Thu Nov 5, 5:00 PM
item.description:
Rattle Creek BBQ is here to stay!
Join us for the grand opening of Rattle Creek BBQ, our new onsite food truck serving up Cali-Mex meets Texas BBQ in the mountains. Owner Mat spent years cooking in Austin, where he fell hard for low-and-slow brisket and bright, fresh flavors. He brought both to Asheville, and the result is a plate that’s rich, smoky, and insanely delicious! Expect BBQ plates, sandwiches, and tacos built around brisket, spare ribs, and pulled pork, with sides like guajillo crunch slaw, elote corn salad, and queso mac & cheese. To celebrate, we’ve got live bluegrass from Andrew Wakefield and friends, free brisket samples while they last, and drink specials all night. Come hungry, bring your friends, and help us give Rattle Creek a proper mountain welcome.
Source: The Mule at Devils Foot

item.description:
PechaKucha Night Returns in November for Volume 43 at The Mule!
PechaKucha Night Asheville is an evening of presentations by the most creative and interesting people in our city, all following the beautifully simple PechaKucha 20×20 format: 20 images, shown for 20 seconds each. With 400 seconds to tell their story, each unique presentation is succinct. You never know what you’ll learn or who you’ll see at PechaKucha. Learn more at https://pechakuchaavl.org, on Instagram @pechakuchaavl, or on Facebook at https://www.facebook.com/pknavl.

item.title: Rumbling Bald Trail; a Saunter — Tue Nov 10, 9:45 AM
item.description: Hendo Fun Friends The Rumbling Bald Trail is a loop trail that meanders through a beautiful hardwood forest along the south face of Rumbling Bald Mountain, revealing huge boulder fields and the base of the cliff areas. These are the cliffs that can be seen from Lake Lure. Remember - hikes led by Gordie tend to have pleasant surprises. Difficulty: Moderate: well developed trail with undulating gradual climbs w natural trail surface. Some stone stairs. Some steep sections. Due to recent events, Bigfoot discussions are no longer permitted. We are the Sloth Hike Team of WNC: “We will get there when we get there.” We dare to go where the ‘real’ hike groups don’t !! **https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TQ8H4EK2vt4** **Details:** Distance: 2.5 mile Loop; Accum ascent: 500ft; Pace: **1.5mph** Drive time: 3/4hr/35 miles (one way) Google map = “Rumbling Bald Access, Lake Lure, NC” Return Not earlier than: 3.00 PM **Optional: Lunch in Chimney Rock (add 1.5 hrs)** Carpool contributions appreciated. $

item.title: Mountain Shag Club — Tue Nov 10, 6:00 PM
item.description:
Come Dance! The Mountain Shag Club was formed in 1988 as a non-profit corporation and is currently a member of the Association of Carolina Shag Clubs. The Mountain Shag CLub was formed with the purpose of bringing people together for fellowship and entertainment, promote the revival and preservation of beach music and shagging, and participate in civic and charitable sanctions and events.
The Carolina Shag is a smooth swing style dance performed to beach music. It is the official state popular dance of North Carolina and the official state dance of South Carolina. The Carolina Shag traces its roots back to the 1940s along the shoreline of the Atlantic Ocean around North Myrtle and Carolina Beach region.
Free. Open to All Ages.
Source: The Mule at Devils Foot

item.title: Artemis Collective Wild Pages Society Book Club — Thu Nov 12, 6:00 PM
item.description: Bring Your Own Book. We’ll bring the people, the chaos, and a new local spot to hang out in. We’re putting a little twist on the traditional book club. No assigned book. No required reading. No guilt if you haven’t read a single page this week. Instead, bring whatever book you’re currently reading and come hang with us. THE 2-HOUR FORMULA First 30 minutes — SOCIALIZE Grab a drink, meet new people, talk books, make friends, and settle in. Next 60 minutes — READ Everyone pulls out their own book and we have a cozy hour of reading together. Think communal reading date, but with your new bookish friends. Last 30 minutes — THE CHAOS Every meetup ends differently. We might play a ridiculous bookish game, make a craft, swap books, shop from a local creator, have a mini book discussion, or just hang out and talk about what we’re reading. And here’s the fun part… WE’RE MOVING AROUND. Every meetup will be hosted at a different local small business around Asheville + WNC. Coffee shops.

item.title: FUEGO Metal Fest — Fri Nov 13, 4:00 PM
item.description:
Get Ready To Experience The Fire, Creativity, And Raw Artistry Of Metal In All Its Forms! FUEGO Metal Fest is a celebration of the incredible artists and metalsmiths who shape, forge, weld, hammer, and transform metal into extraordinary works of art throughout Western North Carolina. From the roar of the forge to the intricate details of handmade jewelry, this festival brings together the region’s metalworking community for an unforgettable showcase of craftsmanship and all things metal. Experience live blacksmithing and forge demonstrations, discover one-of-a-kind jewelry and metal sculptures from talented metalsmiths, and meet the artists behind the work. Whether you’re a seasoned metal head, an art enthusiast, a curious creator, or simply someone who appreciates the beauty of handmade work, there’s something here for you. If it’s made of metal, forged in fire, shaped by hand, or inspired by the art of making, it belongs here. Free to attend.
Source: The Mule at Devils Foot
